name: Denny
tagline: Small wins, lots of accounts, and compounding — one trade per account per day, 10 points at a time, until $4.9K of eval fees compounds into $67K of payouts.
summary: Denny ("Denny Dollas") is a BDH trading-floor trader who trades Nasdaq (NQ) futures almost exclusively across 20+ prop firm accounts — Apex, Tradeify, Lucid, My Funded Futures, IQ Capital, Vest and more — usually one account at a time. His system runs off the 5-minute chart: chop-box scalps for 10-point base hits, the "Two in the Chamber" sweep reversal at strict 1:1, and the Globex first-candle strategy trailed by two units of risk. His golden rule — one trade per account per day, walk away win or lose — turned $4,992 of eval fees into $67,468 of payouts in a single quarter.
oneLiner: Mark 5-minute levels, take one trade per account per day, bank 10-point base hits and 1:1 reversals across 20+ prop accounts, then physically walk away.
keyQuote: One trade per account, per day. Win or lose, that account is done.
keyQuoteSource: One Trade Per Account Per Day: Why I Walk Away
highlights: One trade per account, per day — win or lose, that account is locked for the next 24 hours, and he physically walks away from the screens.
Always use a stop loss: the one time he skipped it cost him a live account plus $3,000 of his own payout money.
Strict 1:1 risk-to-reward on reversals — on NQ a 1:1 is already $300–$400, and 'going for more than that is just getting greedy.'
Scalp the chop box: draw the range on the 5-minute only, execute on the 1-minute, take 10 points ($200) a pop, and stop on the first close outside the box.
Never trade news candles or election nights — that sequence cost him -$4,000 and two Apex accounts in a single session.
The business model: small wins, lots of accounts, and compounding — $4,992 of eval fees became $67,468 of payouts in one quarter.

videos.title: I Lost My Lucid And Tradeify Live Accounts
videos.takeaway: Denny loses both of his live accounts on stream. No strategy detail in the description — the blog article covers the tilt post-mortem.

videos.title: One Trade Per Account Per Day: Why I Walk Away
videos.takeaway: After blowing two BluSky accounts copy trading, sizing up, and chasing what the rest of the desk was doing, he reinstates the golden rule: one trade per account per day, win or lose, then close everything. With 20+ accounts that means ~5 trades a day on the accounts closest to a payout or a pass.

videos.title: Why I Shouldn't Have Traded Election Night
videos.takeaway: Stopped out -$700 in the first minute of election night, then got it back on a Two in the Chamber (+$705). The full ledger: a 400-point textbook bear flag in 35 minutes, a 1,000-point W retrace, and a three-bar reversal worth $20,000 for those who held it.

videos.title: I Lost My Live Account And My Own $3,000
videos.takeaway: Up $1,000, said out loud he was done, then took one more FOMO trade in a perfectly trending market with no stop loss — losing the Lucid live account plus $3,000 of his own payout money. On $2,000-drawdown live accounts: micros only, five max.

videos.title: Don't Start Scalping Until You Watch This!
videos.takeaway: The chop-box system end to end: mark the range wick-to-wick on the 5-minute only (multiple taps at the highs and lows are the tell), drop to the 1-minute to execute, and take 10 points a time — five scalps = $1,000. Stop on the first candle that closes outside the box.

videos.title: I Broke Every Rule I Have Today
videos.takeaway: The Globex first-candle strategy worked (+$700), then a full rule-breaking cascade: no trail on a 10–15 point winner, a -$4,000 news-candle long that blew two Apex accounts, and FOMO top buys (-$1,000, -$500). "I didn't follow my strategies. Didn't follow my discipline. Didn't follow my risk management plan."

videos.title: How I Trade Chop (And When I Just Don't)
videos.takeaway: Chop is one condition — consolidation — and a wick through the level is not a break; only a close is. Either don't trade it ("there's no obligation to be in the market while it's ranging") or buy low and sell high for 10–20 points, taking the scalp and getting out every time.

videos.title: I Took 4 Payouts In One Day On Vest Markets
videos.takeaway: Vest's perpetual mechanics: static 6% max drawdown, and claims are instant and irrevocable — once claimed, the money is no longer at risk even if the account later breaches. He bought two accounts, took four payouts, lost one afterward, and still got paid.

articles.title: One Trade Per Account Per Day: Why I Walk Away
articles.takeaway: His golden anti-overtrading rule: after one trade on an account — win or loss — that account is locked for 24 hours. With 20+ accounts he targets ~5 trades a day on the ones closest to payout/pass, then physically walks away.

articles.title: Why I Shouldn't Have Traded Election Night
articles.takeaway: Election volatility whip-sawed his long for an instant -$700. The mechanical setups paid those who followed them: a three-bar reversal risking ~$1,000 with a potential $20,000, and Two in the Chamber risking $885 for $3,000 through the 1,000-point dump and W reversal.

articles.title: I Lost My Live Account And My Own $3,000
articles.takeaway: Full tilt post-mortem: up $1,000, he took a FOMO re-entry with no stop loss and blew his Lucid Live account plus a personal $3,000 brokerage account. Live-money psychology differs from evals; on small live accounts "stick to 5 micros maximum."

articles.title: Don't Start Scalping Until You Watch This!
articles.takeaway: The Chop Box system: draw the range on the 5-minute only (multiple taps are the tell), execute on the 1-minute, and take strict 10-point ($200) scalps. Five scalps = $1,000/hour; even after the box breaks with one -10pt stop, the day finishes +$800.

articles.title: I Lost Accounts For The First Time In Months
articles.takeaway: On a 700-point NQ flush day the Globex Strategy (first 5-min candle direction) made $1,000 — a properly trailed version risked $1,600 for ~$13,000. Rule: trail the take-profit by two units of risk in expansion markets.

articles.title: I Broke Every Rule I Have Today
articles.takeaway: The Globex Strat (+$700) was his only win before a rule-breaking cascade: no trail on a 10–15 pt winner, a -$4,000 news-candle long that blew two Apex accounts, and FOMO top buys. Salvaged +$1,000 on a VWAP-rejection short — "If you don't follow your risk management plan, the market will make you pay."

articles.title: How I Trade Chop (And When I Just Don't)
articles.takeaway: Chop is consolidation building energy for a breakout, and the break direction after a trend is a reversal signal. Either don't trade it at all — "the absolute easiest way to trade chop is to not touch a button" — or play only the extreme boundaries for 10–20 point base hits.

articles.title: I Took 4 Payouts In One Day On Vest Markets
articles.takeaway: Vest's perpetual accounts: static 6% max drawdown, instant irrevocable claims, unlimited per day. He took four payouts in a day, lost an account afterward, and the payouts still cleared.

articles.title: What I Spent On Prop Firms vs What I Made
articles.takeaway: 90-day ledger transparency: $4,992 spent, $67,468 paid out, $62,476 net (July $1,357 → $25,430; August $25,986; September $1,172 → $16,052). "Small wins, lots of accounts, and compounding."

articles.title: The Easiest Prop Firm Evals To Pass
articles.takeaway: Eval-easiness ranking: Tradeify 50K Growth (no consistency rule, soft $1,250 DLL, news allowed — but never hedge), MFFU Builder, Lucid Flex 50K, and Take Profit Trader 50K, whose no-DLL design he warns will let undisciplined traders blow the account in one day.

articles.title: I Broke My Own Rules And It Worked
articles.takeaway: After a -$200 stop he "loaded the boat" with 5 contracts on a 300K Apex out of frustration and scalped +$1,000 — then publicly condemns emotion-sizing. Also a Two in the Chamber short +$800 and three Tradeify payouts ($2,400).

articles.title: Why Most Traders Fail (And How The Army Fixed My Trading)
articles.takeaway: Discipline framework: accept losing before the session and sit and wait for A+ setups — army "hurry up and wait" gave him the patience edge. Three pillars: risk-to-reward fit to personality, mastering ONE strategy, and waiting as the hardest, most profitable part of the job.

articles.title: I Tried To Trade The News And Got Cooked
articles.takeaway: Bull flags +$200/+$415 and a disciplined chop sit-out, then a news-candle gamble on a fresh eval account hit the $1,000 daily loss limit. Key process: the gamble was isolated to a single account so the copied portfolio stayed green.

articles.title: This Is Exactly How I Set Up My TradingView Chart To Day Trade
articles.takeaway: Chart tutorial: Killzones session boxes/pivots, 9/21 EMAs, and VWAP, with the Long/Short Position tool pre-mapping exact SL/TP (21-point risk, drag to 1:1) and on-chart text journaling ("Risking $500 to make $500 (1:1)").

articles.title: One Long Turned My Worst Morning Green
articles.takeaway: Down $5,600 by mid-morning, one 50-point NY-open long via the trade copier across the portfolio produced ~$19,000 gross → +$12,251 net. He also stopped an IQ account at +$988 "to respect their consistency rule."

articles.title: IQ Capital: Everything You Need To Know Before You Buy
articles.takeaway: Firm review (Standard 50K $49, Rapid, Instant $349) with the key advice: no buffer is required, but "always build a buffer first to protect your account" because trailing drawdown floors move up.

articles.title: FTMO Futures Review: Lose As Much As You Make
articles.takeaway: Growth 50K ($119, 40% consistency, 50% buffer rule) vs Pro 50K ($139 — the "1-to-1" account: $3,000 drawdown matching the $3,000 target, but a hard $1,000 daily loss that terminates the account, his only dislike).

articles.title: I Trade One Account At A Time. Here's Why
articles.takeaway: He cycles accounts one at a time "to manage risk and keep my focus sharp," using the copier only for the highest-conviction trade (opening 9/21-EMA short across 4–5 Apex accounts, +$4,000). Momentum-flip long (5-min close above both EMAs + 9/21 cross) +$2,000.

articles.title: How to Trade Kill Zones Like a Pro
articles.takeaway: His core indicator, Kill Zones and Pivots: session boxes plus auto-plotted Asia/London/NY highs/lows, PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL with statistical hit rates (Asia Low 78% over 41 sessions). Levels are take-profit magnets and stop hiders; a tagged level is dead liquidity.

articles.title: Lost $900, Then This Happened: A Profitable Comeback
articles.takeaway: London chop ground him to -$435, then a high-conviction wick-rejection + tight-consolidation long at 6 contracts → +$2,000, ending +$986. Sizing up only after conviction returns, never after tilt.

articles.title: Apex Changed Every Rule. Is It Still Worth It in 2026?
articles.takeaway: Apex's March 2026 revamp: no MAE or 5:1 rules, no payout denials, built-in scaling, 50% consistency, up to 20 funded accounts, and 1-day eval passes. Choose Intraday vs EOD trailing drawdown (EOD safer but ~2x price); the new $1,000 DLL "actually saves you from blowing the entire account on tilt."

articles.title: Learning Bear Flags Live: My Full London Session Recap
articles.takeaway: Seven live flag trades with the core mechanics on display: trend first, prior-high rejection as confirmation, break-and-close entry — plus a FOMO "I was just guessing" reversal for -$200 as the counter-example.

articles.title: How I Caught These 3 Futures Setups: Daily Trade Recap
articles.takeaway: Two in the Chamber long taken 1:1 for +$770 ("if I had held… a massive $2,385 run — but I stuck to my rules"), a bear-flag scalp +$200, and the 3:50 PM MOC short mirroring the 9:30 candle +$600. Announced his 20-Apex-account copy-trading challenge.

articles.title: My Funded Futures Review: Why Most Traders Pick the Wrong Plan
articles.takeaway: MFFU plans compared: Builder ($63, choose your drawdown), Rapid (funded switches to intraday trail — build a $2,100 buffer first), and Pro ($133, his favorite — funded means no consistency rules and no payout caps). Live triggers: $20K buffer, 3 consecutive payouts, or $100K lifetime.

articles.title: Lucid Trading Review: Pro vs Flex vs Daily vs Direct
articles.takeaway: Lucid's customizable 50Ks: Daily (intraday trail, daily payouts to $8,000), Flex (EOD trail, funded scaling 2→3→4 minis by profit tier), and Pro (1-day pass but 40% consistency funded, $2,100 payout buffer, DLL scales to 60% of EOD balance).

articles.title: Tradeify Just Changed Their Payout Caps (Sept 1st)
articles.takeaway: Flex payout cap cut $3,000 → $2,500 per 5 days; Daily account cap raised $1,000 → $1,250/day ("a massive W… like we do [trade]"); new add-ons buy a 2-day pass with a 50% consistency rule.

articles.title: Every Trade I Took On A Bearish NQ Night
articles.takeaway: Eight trades in a heavy downtrend (price below 9 EMA, 21 EMA, and VWAP all night), from +$2,000 down to -$200 each. Lesson: in a clean trend, trade the flags with size and let momentum work — and "Don't anticipate the candle; wait for it to close!"

articles.title: BluSky Trading: Why You Should Care About This Firm
articles.takeaway: BluSky plans: Launch 200K static-DD, Propel 50K, Orbit 50K (1-day pass, $500 payouts every 3 days), and Instant — a firm founded on removing payout wait barriers.

articles.title: Tradeify Prop Firm Breakdown: Costs, Rules & Payouts Explained!
articles.takeaway: Tradeify 50K plans: Growth ($87, funded 35% consistency — restrictive), Select ($99, his favorite — no DLL in eval; funded Daily = $1,000 payout every day, no consistency), Lightning instant (20% consistency — "I absolutely hate that rule"). He made $5,000 on one Daily account before blowing it.

articles.title: We Were Down $400… Then Made It All Back (Trade Recap)
articles.takeaway: Two chopped-out shorts and a break-even bailout = -$400, then a Silver Two in the Chamber 1:1 winner and a final NQ short at the round 30,000 → +$600. Cut risk early, switch markets when NQ chops, strict 1:1 ("a 1:1 win is a win").

articles.title: I Made $2,000 Trading The Asia Open (Full Recap)
articles.takeaway: Asia-open playbook: 9 EMA + 21 EMA + VWAP aligned bearish with the round "500 level" below as a magnet. A 10-second scalp +$400, then 15 minutes through "trickery" between the EMAs until a candle closed above 21 EMA/VWAP — ~$1,000 on one account in 30 minutes, +$2,000 across accounts.

articles.title: Don't Buy a Prop Account Until You Watch This
articles.takeaway: Educational keystone: account size labels are marketing — the drawdown is your real account size (25K=$1,000, 50K=$2,000, 100K=$3,000, 150K=$4,500). Static vs EOD vs trailing explained; "Take your profits when trading a trailing drawdown!"

articles.title: What Is a Prop Firm? Here's How It Actually Works
articles.takeaway: Prop-firm primer on the three phases (evaluation → sim-funded → live) and $50–$150 fees, with the honesty check: re-buying blown evals "is just gambling… feeding the firm's business model"; "the account size is never the hard part. The discipline is."

articles.title: 2 in the Chamber: The NQ Reversal Setup I Actually Trade
articles.takeaway: His signature setup, fully specified: two consecutive 5-min candles making new session extremes, then a trigger candle that sweeps another extreme and closes opposite-colored; enter next candle open, stop one tick beyond the trigger wick, strict 1:1 ($300–$400 on NQ). Trade Asia/London/NY; skip Globex 6–8 PM.
